correctness.rationale: For p=r, Frobenius yields (X−1)^(r^a). Otherwise the degree multiset has one 1 and φ(r^j)/ord_{r^j}(p) copies of the order at each level. The contiguous-subset lemma, the order-lifting identities with v_r(p−1) or v_r(p+1), and a separate odd-r obstruction prove exact coverage/first gap for all primes and exponents. For r=2 the Euler-phi order bound suffices. The density conclusion counts r+1 reduced classes modulo r² and uses PNT in AP. The provided script passed 1242 order-based exhaustive-degree checks and 242 independently factored polynomial checks; finite tests only corroborate, not prove, the infinite claim.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Thompson’s general factor-degree representation is a decision criterion on arbitrary indices but does not give a closed congruence description of the full prime-power family. Its explicit sufficient ±1 modulo the entire index classes cover only a subset of the claimed admissible classes when a≥3, and its equal-characteristic lemma covers p=r. The published φ-practical and lambda-star practical results concern different divisor notions and do not imply this finite-field prime-characteristic classification.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior special cases p=r and p≡±1 mod r^a imply only some successful inputs; n=r=5 is cited as a known example, not rediscovered. Conversely, the theorem does not subsume Thompson’s general-index criterion or general density estimates, and does not concern polynomial divisors over Z[X].

originality.rationale: Targeted primary-source and published-results comparisons identify Thompson’s general p-practical multiplicative-order criterion and the sufficient ±1 mod n classes, but not the simultaneous prime-power exponent-stable exact congruence classification, sharp least missing degrees, and prime-density formula. Generic algorithmic expressibility does not state those closed-form results. The fully read relevant theorem statements and algorithms were compared by logical implication. An unindexed or overlooked direct corollary remains a risk.
residual_risks: The specialized classification may already occur in unindexed notes or be treated as a standard exercise following the generic criterion; the primary thesis and journal do not visibly state it in the inspected relevant sections.
The literature comparison is not independently audited; some long source documents were inspected by relevant sections and full-text searches rather than every proof line.

value.rationale: Prime-power indices are an intrinsic and non-arbitrary first case of the established p-practical cyclotomic divisor-degree problem. A complete closed congruence classification, sharp first failing degree for each disallowed characteristic, stabilization at exponent 2, and exact density across varying characteristics are genuinely useful arithmetic structural information beyond finite examples or a generic decision criterion. They guide extensions to composite indices and distributional questions without assuming such extensions have been proved.
